title: The Creative Industries: How Sora and text to video is redefining the creative landscape
description: Send us Fan Mail Is it already the end of the road for CGI, animation studios and graphic designers? Join us for our first industry focussed episode as we scrutinize the latest awe-inspiring yet potentially unsettling advancements in artificial intelligence impacting the creative industries. Our latest episode peels back the curtain on Sora, OpenAI's newest marvel, capable of crafting lifelike videos from simple text prompts. We wrestle with the excitement and trepidation that such innovation stirs within the creative community, contemplating how the potential of AI can be balanced with the pressing ethical dilemmas it poses. As always we focus on AI's influence on job security, and how it is already reshaping the creative industry's landscape—from animation to graphic design. We discuss concrete examples such as the recent decison to put an $800m studio development on hold. We're candid about the challenges that lie ahead, particularly for the middle-tier professionals whose careers may be most vulnerable to AI's cost-effective solutions. Simultaneously, we extend a hand to guide you through the looming transformation, offering perspectives on how to embrace AI tools and adapt your career path in an industry on the brink of a revolution.
summary: Episode two confronts Sora: both hosts are awed by text-to-video's leap from incoherent five-second clips to believable one-minute films, and Tyler Perry's $800m studio-expansion pause lands as a canary in the coal mine. They weigh democratized creativity against disinformation, conclude watermarking will fail against open source, and forecast prompt-to-feature-film within 12 months and creative-sector job losses within five years — advising creatives to familiarize themselves with the tools while planning several career pivots.
keyTalkingPoints: Sora blew minds: from rough 5-second clips a year ago to cohesive, near-real one-minute video — roughly a 10x length gain per year
Tyler Perry put an $800m VFX studio investment on hold immediately after Sora — 'future jobs lost' and a canary in the mine
Democratization upside: anyone can create films and stories; downside: watermarks will not hold once open-source models catch up
Stable Diffusion now spells words correctly most of the time; transformers and diffusion models are different technologies converging on creative work
Writers' strike won a reprieve (ChatGPT restricted) but the hosts see layoffs arriving via drip, not announcement
Practical advice: upskill into the tools now, but treat that as a temporary bridge — expect to retrain several times

jimmy: Sora-level video democratizes creativity but supercharges disinformation — AI already lurks in YouTube comments and Twitter roasts
Tyler Perry's pause shows incumbents see the writing on the wall; full-length AI feature films arrive within 12 months
Job losses in creative sectors within five years, though not mass layoffs in the next 12 months
Stopping AI is not in the realms of reality — individuals must plan for how it affects them
matt: Initial reaction was 'wow, but so what' — until the job implications in effects, animation and VFX became clear
Digital watermarks are not a long-term solution; the 16-year-old with an open-source model circumvents them
Hand-made human art endures — he values his daughter's drawings more because of AI images
Expect no announcements: layoffs will come as unfilled positions and drip-drip opportunity loss
